activity_context.topic_title: Double Integrals Over Type I Regions

feedback.problem: If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the curves $y=2x$ and $y={x}^{2},$ then ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA=$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's make a sketch of our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14100085/assets/c8cf45693dbf89b4f2b5efda32904d07d8205770419cc5ffdec63f4b43c0e145.png)

Now, let's represent $D$ as a type I region. 

- To determine the $x$-limits, we need to find the $x$-coordinates of the points at which the curves intersect. So, we set the following equation and solve it for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & =2x \\ {x}^{2}-2x & =0 \\ x(x-2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x$-limits are 
$0\le x\le 2.$

- To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14100085/assets/14d0f60200b6efee0de1611a51a71e27eb6070697cb02db58007b52a8b3f172d.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 2x}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2x}f(x,y)\text{ }dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{2x}f(x,y)\text{ }dy]dx\end{aligned}
$$
